proposals.name: Gravosk
proposals.entry:
Homeland: The Gravoska Kingdom
Known For: Great physical mass, horns, oral history, formidable law, the Muster, longboats, and Thunder-Mead
Common Saying: “Gravosk never forgets.”

The Gravosk are a broad, heavily built horned people native to the high mountains and northern forests of the Gravoska Kingdom. They are shorter than the Veyr but considerably heavier, with dense bones, immense shoulders, thick hands, shaggy hair, and horns that vary greatly between individuals.

Continuance

The central Gravosk philosophy is Continuance. Everything breaks. Ships sink. Tools wear out. Houses burn. People die. The worthy response is not to pretend otherwise, but to make certain that what matters continues afterward.

A repaired tool is respected. A master who dies without training a replacement has failed. A commander who wins today’s battle while making tomorrow’s impossible has failed.

The traditional compliment is: “They left less unfinished than they found.”

Gravosk Never Forgets

Debts, insults, murders, gifts, kindnesses, rescues, meals given in hard winters, and promises fulfilled are remembered with extraordinary persistence. An obligation may pass from parent to child if it remains unsettled. Equally important, once a matter is properly settled, continuing the dispute is itself dishonorable.

Gravosk never forgets that something was settled either.

Strangers

Gravosk are not automatically generous toward foreigners. A stranger can expect lawful treatment, honest bargaining, and whatever hospitality custom specifically requires. Trust is earned slowly. Once earned, however, it may survive generations. Their exceptional relationship with the Drusha began during the Winter of 176.

Oral Culture and Law

Writing is common in administration and commerce, but important history is expected to live in people. Genealogies, legal judgments, treaties, debts, battles and family histories are preserved through structured recitation. The greatest practitioners are the Battle Poets.

Gravosk law is old, elaborate and rigorous. A common maxim says: “A law too complicated to remember was written to deceive.” Justice often asks not simply who is guilty, but: What remains unsettled?

Death

The Gravosk speak comfortably about death. A long life is admirable; a completed life is more important. Funeral speakers mention failures as well as virtues. Unfinished obligations are spoken aloud and relatives may publicly assume them. Then Thunder-Mead is poured upon the funeral pyre. The dead burn. The living drink.

Common Roles

Foresters, shipwrights, armorers, bombard crews, pyre-beekeepers, brewers, judges, Witnesses, hunters, mountain guides, herders, smiths, sailors and soldiers are common professions. Nearly every adult also owes service through the Muster.

posts.name: Gamemaster Only
posts.entry:
An old Gravosk genealogy contains a name deliberately removed from every later recitation. Deliberately causing the Gravosk to forget a person may be one of the most serious crimes imaginable.

A respected Gravosk family has spent six generations repaying a favor that the supposed recipient’s descendants know nothing about. Someone misunderstood the original obligation—but admitting that now could ruin several powerful families.
